title: Affined question: dispositions preparing for justification
source_text: XLVIII. Idemque judicium faciendum videtur de affini controversia, An scilicet homo peccator quibusdam operibus ad justificationem praeparetur & disponatur? quod similiter docent & tuentur Pontificii, Protestantes vero negant. Nam quum istud affirmant Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, mens eorum alia non est, quam Deum, prius-quam hominem peccatorem Spiritu suo sanctificante donet, illique fidei, spei, & cha-ritatis, aliarumque virtutum Christianarum habitus infundat, consuevisse illum gratia sua praevenire, per quam in eo quosdam actus excitat fidei, spei, & dilectionis, ut timoris judicii divini, doloris de peccato, & propositi novae vitae, & si qui sunt similes, qui sunt veluti quaedam conditiones praeviae, & morales dispositiones, sine quibus Deus non solet Spiritum illum suum in peccatores effundere.
pass_a_gloss: And the same judgment seems to be made about the kindred controversy: Whether a sinful man is prepared and disposed for justification by certain works?—which likewise the Papists teach and defend, but the Protestants deny. For when the doctors of the Roman Church affirm that, their mind is no other than that God, before he endows a sinful man with his sanctifying Spirit and infuses into him the habits of faith, hope, and charity and of the other Christian virtues, has been accustomed to prevent him by his grace, by which he excites in him certain acts of faith, hope, and love, as of fear of divine judgment, sorrow for sin, and purpose of a new life, and whatever are like these, which are as it were certain prior conditions and moral dispositions without which God is not accustomed to pour out that Spirit of his upon sinners.
pass_b_english: Affined dispute: is the sinner prepared by certain works for justification? Rome yes, Protestants no—in words.
Rome means preventing grace excites prior acts of faith, hope, love, fear, sorrow, new-life purpose as conditions before habitual infusion.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1082.
